group.passage:
Does making food out of thin air raise your eyebrows? The world’s first “air-protein,” called Solein and created by the Finnish start-up Solar Foods, received approval from the Singapore Food Agency in 2022. This year, the company launched its commercial-scale Factory 01 in Finland, with plans to introduce products to the EU and US markets by 2025. Solein, a mustard-yellow powder, is a pure and nutritious protein containing all essential amino acids.
Solar Foods produces Solein using sophisticated machines powered by solar energy. The process involves feeding microbes with carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen extracted from the air. This bioprocess essentially resembles yogurt or wine fermentation with sugar replaced by these gases. Solein production is the first food production method entirely independent of agriculture.
Studies have pointed out that agriculture contributes to approximately 30% of greenhouse gas emissions and 70% of global water use, with negative impacts such as land degradation and waterway pollution. In contrast, Solein production requires just 10% of the land and 1% of the water needed for producing an equivalent amount of meat protein, with only 1% of the associated greenhouse gas emissions. It also eliminates the need for fertile land, animals, or photosynthetic plants, which makes it uniquely scalable. Production can occur anywhere, including harsh environments like deserts, Arctic regions, and even space.
Moreover, Solein’s versatility allows it to take on various shapes and flavors. With Solein incorporated into affordable foods, we will only need one-tenth of the current agricultural land yet produce sufficient protein-rich foods to meet global demands. Consequently, Solein is increasingly seen as a solution to climate change and food scarcity. Also, its potential for space-based production could support long-term space missions, enabling more effective human exploration of the universe.
As Solar Foods pioneers this revolutionary method, other alternative proteins derived from plants, cells, or microorganisms also promise sustainable food production. Tomorrow’s menu might include dairy products made from fermented milk cells, plant-based desserts enriched with milk fat, or bioreactor-produced chicken breast filets. The world is swiftly approaching a global food production transformation aimed at feeding the growing population sustainably.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.A: Solein production uses 100 times less water and 10 times less land than animal farming.
options.B: Solein is created by feeding microbes with gases from the air, using sugar as a nutrient.
options.C: Solein comes in a form of mustard-yellow powder, which can only be consumed directly.
options.D: Solar Foods plans to limit Solein production to areas with tropical climates and barren soils.

questions.stem: How does solar food production compare to agriculture?

options.A: It requires more land and water but emits less greenhouse gas.
options.B: They both depend heavily on land conditions and water availability.
options.C: They both require animal and photosynthetic plants to produce protein.
options.D: It is independent of fertile land and can occur in extreme environments.

questions.stem: Where is the text most likely to be found?

options.A: In an advertisement for a new restaurant menu item.
options.B: In a scientific research paper on farming practices.
options.C: In a journal focused on cutting-edge food innovation.
options.D: On a website discussing pros and cons of scientific advancement.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is an opinion, NOT a fact?

options.A: Tomorrow’s menu might include dairy products created through advanced sustainable methods.
options.B: The process of making Solein basically mimics traditional fermentation methods.
options.C: Solein production is more energy-efficient than animal or plant-based food production.
options.D: The scalability and independence from fertile land make Solein a solution for food production.
